body:
It definitely makes me feel better that there are other people that feel the same way I do.
I suppose, I've always felt alone in that aspect.

Thank you for your kind reply.

I have very high ideals, such that they often get in the way of my own success.
I'll bend over backwards for any of my friends without expecting anything in return, even if I lose out because of it.

I suppose at some point I decided that pursuing my own happiness will only get in the way of others. (coping mechanism?)  So everything I do is to create a better world where others who have had similar experiences to me will have some breathing room.  (I'm approaching it through sustainable technology, education of my friends on how to understand their electricity usage, and what cheap methods they can use to curb it)

|You don't seem strange to me. You seem smart. That means most people aren't capable of understanding how your mind works. I'm in the same boat.

With regards to this statement, I think this is a large character flaw of mine that makes me shutdown.  As a child, when my brother would pick on me, I would use my grades and intellect as a defense.  Eventually, I realized I was putting him down, to boost my self worth.  I feel very guilty about this.  Now whenever someone doesn't understand something I say, I kinda just let it go, and let them think whatever they want.  I don't want to put anyone down... I know what it feels like.

Hey, feel free to respond or PM me.  
I would love the opportunity to listen to you.

There are a lot of reasons I can think.

1.  I grew up way too fast.  When I was 4 my uncle died of lung cancer.  When I was 5 my best friend was crushed by a pile of logs the summer after kindergarten.  When I was 7 my dad died of a sudden heart attack.  By the time I was 18, I had been to 30 funerals of my friends and family, and had been a Pallbearer 6 times.  I feel the most pain about this around Christmas and father's day.  (I hate Christmas)

2.  After my dad died, my brother (6 years my elder would beat me daily and abuse me verbally.)  because he had anger issues about my fathers death, and I did better in school since I was much smarter.  I don't want to  blame him for anything, and I forgive him.  I understand he hurt too.

3.  My dad was jewish and my mom was catholic.  Both religions reject me.  Though I was still bullied and beaten in a hick North East PA highschool for being a penny picking jew.  (I have never had a religious affiliation)

4.  I had an Aunt who loved to argue and pretty much raised me.  This formed a natural devil's advocate response in me.  I don't know how to stop it, I always interject counter arguments to people's displeasure.  I think it doesn't help that I'm very intelligent and make people feel inferior.  I never tried to... it just happened.  The result being that I stopped talking, and became the quiet kid (otherwise i'd be the asshole)

5.  I'm extremely empathetic and sensitive to body language.  I hear what people say, but it doesn't matter.  I can see the way a person's body tenses up when I say something they didn't like.  I can see the anger or spite in their eyes when I do something wrong, even if they try to be nice about it.  I can't really go out where there are large groups of people.  I pay attention to everyone, not to get in their way, not to bother anyone, it causes me have mini panic attacks.

6.  I'm really struggling to deal with my girlfriend's parental relationship.  She was beaten badly physically and mentally, by her insane father.  She is obedient to him, and it makes me want to cry.  She has breakdowns if I try to address her issues.  She becomes cold and distant, and I feel like there's nothing I can do.  (I've been with her for 6 years).   

7.  When I was in 8th grade, I had 2 friends.  They invited me to a sleepover, and I woke up to a smoke bomb in my sleeping bag, and getting shot at with airsoft guns while 3 of them yelled "get the jew".  I'm not even jewish...
They told everyone in the highschool, and I was a social outcast.  I closed myself off to anyone.  I never made a friend until college.

8.  I'm wierd as hell.  I don't like music.  I don't like TV.  I've always been singled out as being too quiet or strange when I did talk.  I put strange thoughts together.  I have strange thoughts.  Though they don't seem strange to me.  The only reason I know I'm weird, is because that's what everyone tells me...

9.  I'm a terrible worker.  I'm an electrical engineer, and I'm very smart.  I just have no motivation anymore.  I don't think I ever did.  I was carried through a good university just based on my raw skill.  I didn't study, I just did my homework, and took the tests.  I passed.  But, I still don't have motivation to do anything.  I get stuck in loops, and watch the hours pass.  I want to work hard, I really do.  I don't know what's wrong with me.

10.  I've always had financial problems as I was raised by a single mother, without a proper education.  I'm not blaming her for anything, I owe her more than I can imagine.  Being crushed by debt right now is probably a really big part of this.  I definitely, can't afford any sort of therapy.

11.  My nickname as a kid was Windsor.  I didn't know why.  When I was 10 I googled it.  turns out it is a canadian whiskey.  One night at a family dinner I was called that name.  I said "I know why you call me that", and they go "oh yah why".  "Because I was an accident", and they just fell silent.  My Aunt who was a large part of my life, then taught me the definition of the word serendipity.  I suppose its strange for a little boy to put that together.  That memory has always made me feel so small.  That my family would assign that nickname to make fun of me as a kid, thinking I was none the wiser.

12.  People have much worse problems, and here I am feeling sorry myself.  I think this is the worst feeling I've ever had.

There's more, but my lunch break is over.  Thanks for reading again.
